findings.evidence: Rolle.lean:34-83 all five consequences take `(h : Rolle R)`; roadmap README line 29-30 fixes the convention `[Field R] [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] [IsRealClosed R]` for ordered algebraic statements, and lines 193-197 list Rolle and its sign/monotonicity consequences as targets over such `R`.
findings.fix: In `AbstractRolle.lean` (which imports both files) add the `[IsRealClosed R]`-form statements derived from `rolle_realClosed`: mean value and `MonotoneOn`/`AntitoneOn`/`StrictMonoOn`/`StrictAntiOn` of `p.eval` on `Icc a b`; or drop the predicate and state those five results directly under `[IsRealClosed R]`.
findings.issue: `Rolle R` is an abstraction with a single model: `rolle_realClosed` (AbstractRolle.lean:113) proves it for every ordered real closed field and nothing else in the repo proves or could plausibly prove it otherwise. Consequently the roadmap's Layer 1 targets — polynomial Rolle and derivative-sign monotonicity — have no statement at the natural level `[Field R] [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] [IsRealClosed R]`; every use must thread a provable hypothesis.

summary: The mathematics sits at the right level overall, but three statements carry hypotheses stronger than they need (a field where a commutative ring suffices, an order on an order-free statement, a redundant `p ≠ 0`), and the roadmap's Rolle/monotonicity targets exist only relative to the single-model `Rolle R` predicate rather than under `[IsRealClosed R]`.
